resolution: Settled by printed text, read literally: Pure ignores "all other attributes", and the Manual names Tough as an attribute ("4. Attributes like Tough"), so Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware do not apply in a Pure interaction. R61's "stats are not attributes" is our ruling and does not change what the Manual calls Tough. attr.general.pure states print; the engine keeps the stat attributes on: F-U19-1 (CT-260, filed as an owner decision on whether to change the engine). Document fix: done 2026-10-10. attr.pure.stat-attributes (which stated R289) and attr.pure.unaware-combat (which stated R106) contradicted attr.general.pure; both now state print and are marked engine-differs (F-U19-1, F-U19-2). Register fix: mark R289's "still read" sentence and R106's "survives {Pure}" as outranked by the printed reminder.

summary: What Inverted inverts from when a base rewrite is in play: R93 (owner, 2026-08-22) inverts from the rewritten base; the owner's later general answer that any difference from printed stats is a stat change, and a _passer post in #rules-questions, invert from the printed stats instead.

sides.quote: Invert the stat changes of inverted units. For example, -1/+2 would become +1/-2.
(R66) — redefines what base *is*, so it is the thing inverted FROM and is never
> "Inverted looks at Printed base stats, looks what unit is 'currently' and
Literally any change to a unit's stats counts. If they're different from the
Its base stats aren't being inverted. Just the modifications to those stats by counters, stat-altering augments, or attributes.
invert the difference"
"So if there was 10/15 which base stats were changed to be 4/4 (Formless does
this), it had +1/+1 counter, then: 10/15 → 4/4 → 5/5. If you invert it now it
sees that total diff from original stat is -5/-10, so it traces back to

resolution: Question for the owner. The rule follows R93, which the owner ruled on 2026-08-22 with both worked examples in view (the R93 addendum quotes _passer in full). R157 §14, three days later, defines a stat change generally ("If they're different from the printed stats, they are changed"), and Unaware (rule attr.unaware) already reads a base rewrite as a stat change under it. The _passer posts are in #rules-questions, not a [Solved] RAQ write-up, so they do not outrank the owner. If the owner chooses B, the engine change is one line in effStats (79-round17-layers.test.ts names it).

question.ask: Does Inverted invert from the printed stats, or from a rewritten base?

readings.label: A
readings.text: From the rewritten base: a base rewrite is a new base, not a stat change (R93; spikeydog).
readings.table: A 10/15 made base 4/4 with a +1/+1 counter, Inverted, is a 3/3.

readings.label: B
readings.text: From the printed stats: any difference from the printed stats is a stat change (R157 §14; _passer's two posts).
readings.table: The same unit, Inverted, is a 15/25.

question.recommend: B, for one definition of a stat change: the owner's later general words (R157 §14) and _passer agree, and Unaware already reads a base rewrite as a change. Keep A only if R93 was meant as a deliberate exception for Inverted.

summary: Whether a unit without Flying may block a Flying column together with a Flying unit in the same blocking column. The printed reminder names units; the Manual says "the blocking unit"; the Rulebook says "unless the defending player also has flying units"; R248 records that the client "blocks by COLUMN".

sides.quote: Only flying units can block flying units.
blocked unless the blocking unit has flying.
Flying attribute and the entire column cannot be blocked unless the defending player
blocks by COLUMN and the authored row said so.
Its column can only be blocked by a column with Flying.

resolution: Question for the owner. No test plays the shared case and no designer source addresses it: the printed reminder names units, the Manual "the blocking unit", and the Rulebook "the defending player".

question.ask: May a unit without Flying block a Flying column together with a Flying unit in the same blocking column?

readings.label: A
readings.text: Yes: attributes are shared in a column in all situations, so the non-Flying unit has Flying and the column may block.
readings.table: A Flying blocker lets its column-mate join the block.

readings.label: B
readings.text: No: every unit that blocks a Flying column must have Flying itself.
readings.table: A non-Flying unit may never stand in a column blocking Flying.

question.follows: Neither: the rule states only the restriction both readings share. Our glossary row and R248 ("blocks by COLUMN") describe A.
question.recommend: A: Caleb says column-mates share attributes "in all situations" (R93), and A is the permissive reading.

resolution: Follow R281: an Unaware card can be targeted, and stat changes put on it do nothing while it is Unaware. Mark R106's targeting paragraph "(answered by R281)". Still open, and conditional: whether a stat-gated target restriction ("base power 2 or less") reads the printed stats of a non-Unaware target when the effect's source is Unaware. summary: The Tough + Inverted law rests on the owner's retracted bug report and R226's derivation; the owner's own words ("always kills") are stronger than the law R226 pins (a shrunk unit survives).

sides.quote: > works. So tough + inverted always kills the unit since +0/+X is just -0/-X
> ### **final defense = −2Δ.** The base cancels out completely.

resolution: Follow R226: the rule states the law (defense = -2 x the net change), which is the owner's statement for every board where the defense has not been reduced. No designer source; Caleb's nearby remark ("tough inverted would die before you could add more", R93) agrees with the common case.

resolution: Follow R106 (owner) for the scope, with R281 for targeting. Question for the owner only if a comparison CR treats other interactions (an ability that reads another card's stats, a stat-gated target restriction) as "interacting".

summary: Sources silent on whether a Feeble unit may attack or be sent to counterattack. The printed reminder restricts only blocking.

sides.quote: Feeble units can't block.
They are 0/1 units that can't block

resolution: No rule is written beyond "can't block". The literal reading (Feeble restricts nothing else) is the permissive one; question for the owner only if a comparison CR restricts attacking.
